Mechanical Fault.definition: Physical or mechanical abnormality involving moving parts, structural components, or mechanical mechanisms.
examples: Motor producing abnormal vibration.
The motor is making a strange noise.
Motor lo unusual sound vastundi.
The bearing has failed and the motor is making grinding noise.
Shaft misalignment causing violent wobble.
Gear teeth damaged in gearbox.
మోటార్ ఎక్కువగా వైబ్రేట్ అవుతోంది
boundaries: Distinguish from Electrical Fault when motor noise is accompanied by electrical sparking or winding burnout.
Distinguish from Temperature Fault when mechanical friction causes heat as a secondary symptom.
Mechanical Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if problem is purely electrical circuit/wiring or solely abnormal ambient/surface temperature without mechanical vibration or component failure.

Electrical Fault.definition: Abnormality in electrical circuits, wiring, current, voltage levels within components, or electrical contacts.
examples: Short circuit in control panel wiring.
Motor winding burnt due to overcurrent.
Sparking observed at terminal block.
Open circuit in wiring harness.
Voltage drop across terminal connections.
boundaries: Distinguish from Power Supply Fault when the problem is internal circuit failure rather than external incoming power failure.
Distinguish from Mechanical Fault when electrical short causes motor stoppage.
Electrical Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if power is completely absent from the external source or if the root issue is purely mechanical contact noise.

Sensor Fault.definition: Defect or malfunction in a sensor device, sensor connection, calibration, or measurement output accuracy.
examples: Temperature sensor is giving incorrect readings.
Pressure sensor output stuck at zero.
Optical proximity sensor disconnected.
Thermocouple calibration drifted significantly.
Vibration sensor not detecting motion.
boundaries: Distinguish from Temperature Fault when the sensor incorrectly reports temperature but actual equipment temperature is normal.
Distinguish from Mechanical Fault when vibration sensor is faulty rather than the motor.
Sensor Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if physical temperature or vibration is genuinely abnormal and the sensor is correctly reading that abnormal state.

Temperature Fault.definition: Abnormal physical or thermal condition where equipment or environment temperature exceeds or falls outside safe operational thresholds.
examples: Machine temperature is continuously above the safe limit.
Motor overheating during extended continuous run.
Cooling radiator failed causing excessive ambient heat.
Bearing housing temperature exceeding 95 degrees Celsius.
boundaries: Distinguish from Sensor Fault when physical heat is verified and the sensor is functioning properly.
Distinguish from Mechanical Fault when overheating is the primary observed fault without mechanical breakdown.
Temperature Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if the temperature sensor itself is giving erratic or erroneous measurements while physical temperature is normal.

Software Fault.definition: Abnormality in application software, controller firmware, logic execution, program crashes, or digital operating algorithms.
examples: Controller application keeps crashing on startup.
PLC firmware threw fatal memory error.
HMI display frozen on status screen.
Software logic bug causing valve command loop.
Robot controller rebooting during routine execution.
boundaries: Distinguish from Communication Fault when software crashes internally without network or protocol transmission loss.
Software Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if the issue is a physical network disconnection, cable break, or wireless handshake failure.

Power Supply Fault.definition: Failure, absence, or instability in incoming electrical power delivery to the system, power adapter, battery, or power grid feed.
examples: Device is not receiving power from main supply.
24V DC power supply adapter has zero output.
Backup battery discharged and failed to switch over.
Main feeder circuit breaker tripped causing power loss.
Motor stopped because power is not reaching it.
boundaries: Distinguish from Electrical Fault when the external feed or supply unit is interrupted rather than an internal component short circuit.
Power Supply Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if power is being supplied properly but internal device circuits short-circuit or trip internally.

Communication Fault.definition: Failure or degradation in transmission of data, signals, or protocol packets between systems, controllers, or network devices.
examples: ESP32 cannot connect to WiFi access point.
CAN bus communication timeout between drive and controller.
MQTT connection dropped repeatedly.
RS-485 serial link reporting packet loss.
Ethernet link down between PLC and SCADA.
boundaries: Distinguish from Software Fault when communication link or network is the root failure rather than software crash.
Communication Fault.exclusion_guidance: Do not select if software program halted or crashed before attempting communication.

Unknown.definition: Descriptions with insufficient, ambiguous, contradictory, or vague information that cannot reliably be mapped to one specific category.
examples: Something is wrong with the machine.
Machine is behaving strangely.
Motor stopped suddenly.
Line 3 not working properly.
Unit stopped.
boundaries: Use Unknown whenever the input does not provide explicit or sufficient evidence for any specific fault category.
Unknown.exclusion_guidance: Do not use if clear evidence for one of the other 7 categories is present.
